name: first-run
title: Get FabCLI ready to use
summary: Check the session, have the user sign in if needed, and install the Claude Code skill

steps.why: See whether there is a valid Epic session; this never opens a window
steps.check: authenticated is true and fab.session_ok is true: skip the login step

on_error.auth_required: No session yet (or it expired): do the login step

steps.why: Sign in to Epic, about once a year. A window opens for the user (credentials and 2FA); wait for it to exit, allowing a couple of minutes
steps.check: ok is true; with a valid session it returns at once with already_authenticated

steps.why: For Claude Code users: install the FabCLI skill into ~/.claude/skills/fabcli/

on_error.network: The skill mirror on GitHub is unreachable; try later, or install from a local file with --source path=<file>

notes: If fabcli isn't found, it isn't on PATH yet: the user runs install.bat (Windows) or ./install.sh (Linux) in the unpacked release folder, then opens a new terminal. It changes their PATH, so suggest it rather than running it unasked.
Only auth login is interactive. Every other command runs headless.
The token is encrypted on disk; check it with auth status, never by reading the file.
